title: The $50 Million Deal Blockbuster Laughed At

scenes.text: In September two thousand, three men flew to Dallas to sell their company to a giant. The giant said no. Ten years later, the giant was bankrupt.

visual.text: Video giant turns down a $50 million internet start-up

scenes.text: This is the story of the fifty million dollar deal Blockbuster laughed at.

visual.text: The $50 million deal Blockbuster laughed at

scenes.text: It starts in nineteen eighty-five.
The first Blockbuster opened in Dallas, Texas. Bright blue and yellow, thousands of tapes on the wall, open late every night.
By two thousand four, it had about nine thousand stores and roughly eighty-four thousand workers.
Friday night meant a trip to Blockbuster. Almost every town had one.

visual.title: A store in almost every town

scenes.text: But part of the money came from something customers hated. Late fees.

visual.title: Return it late, pay a fee

scenes.text: In two thousand alone, late fees brought in about eight hundred million dollars. Around sixteen percent of all its revenue.
Meanwhile, a tiny company was mailing DVDs in red envelopes.
Netflix was founded in nineteen ninety-seven by Reed Hastings and Marc Randolph. Rent online, get the disc by mail, no late fees.

visual.title: Two ways to rent a movie

scenes.text: But in two thousand, Netflix was losing money. So the founders made a bold pitch.
They flew to Blockbuster's headquarters in Dallas and met its chief executive, John Antioco.
The offer: buy Netflix for fifty million dollars. Netflix would run Blockbuster's website, Blockbuster would keep the stores.
According to Marc Randolph, the Blockbuster team struggled not to laugh. The answer was no.

visual.source: As told by Netflix co-founder Marc Randolph

scenes.text: So the two founders went home and decided to beat Blockbuster instead.
Blockbuster fought back. It dropped late fees and launched its own online rental service in two thousand four. For a while, it worked.
But the stores were expensive, the debt was heavy, and streaming was coming.
In September twenty ten, carrying about a billion dollars of debt, Blockbuster filed for bankruptcy.
The next year, Dish Network bought what was left for three hundred twenty million dollars.
Today, only one Blockbuster is left, in Bend, Oregon. Netflix is worth hundreds of billions.
The lesson. The money you make from annoying your customers is money a competitor will take away.

visual.text: Late fees made Blockbuster rich, and gave Netflix its pitch.
